title: Formation of Lake Tanganyika
summary: Lake Tanganyika lies in the western branch of the East African Rift. A 1993 reflection-seismic and radiocarbon study estimated that the basins of central Lake Tanganyika began forming between 9 and 12 Ma, the northern basin at about 7 to 8 Ma and the southern basin at about 2 to 4 Ma. A 2022 paper adds that the sub-basins fused into the present lake about 5 to 6 million years ago.

uncertainty.note: Central-basin range from Cohen, Soreghan and Scholz (1993); northern basin 7-8 Ma, southern 2-4 Ma; fusion of sub-basins 5-6 Ma. The id says 9 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present.

as_recorded.value: structural basins of central Lake Tanganyika began to form between 9 and 12 Ma
The initial basin was formed around 9–12 million years ago (MYA)

where.modern_name: Lake Tanganyika, Tanzania, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Burundi and Zambia (lake-centre proxy)
where.historical_name: Western Rift basin of the East African Rift, Late Miocene; no polities exist

paleo.note: Lake-centre proxy at 10 Ma. MULLER2019 gives 7.85 S, 27.30 E and PALEOMAP 6.54 S, 28.66 E.

importance.justification: One of the deepest and oldest rift lakes, with basins that formed at different times.

reviewer_note: The 9-12 Ma range is for the central basin only and comes from the 1993 RSRM method; rift-initiation timing is not firmly settled. The 2022 paper is a fish-genetics study that restates the geology.
